about: The order a table's rows show in (LANGUAGE.md, Tables: order by and sortable), the same on every renderer: the web's Svelte part and the Avalonia control are both run through these cases. A table has its rows in the order of the data; `order` is the table's first order (order by field [desc]), `sortable` lets a click on a header sort by that column, and a second click on it sorts the other way. Sorting changes only how the rows show: a row keeps its place in the data, so events and the chosen row name the row by that place. Text sorts ignoring case, numbers as numbers, a choice (an enum or a reference) by the label it shows; an empty value comes last either way, and rows that are equal keep the order of the data. Steps: click a shown row (counted from the top as shown), sort by a column (a click on its header). Expected: the rows as shown, top to bottom, by their place in the data; the events ('select 2' when the row at place 2 of the data is chosen); the chosen row by its place in the data.

cases.name: without an order the rows show as the data has them
numbers sort as numbers, with an empty value last
an empty value comes last the other way too
a choice sorts by the label it shows
a click on a sortable header sorts by that column
a second click on the header sorts the other way
a click on another header sorts by that one, first ascending
without sortable a click on a header changes nothing
a row clicked in sorted order is chosen by its place in the data
sorting is no select and the chosen row stays chosen
